translations.text: This is John's testimony, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
These things happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
He said to them, “Come and see.” So they came and saw where he was staying, and they stayed with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.
His mother said to the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
The Jews said to him, “It took forty-six years to build this temple, and you will raise it up in three days?”
While Jesus was in Jerusalem at the Passover festival, many believed in him because they saw the signs he was performing.
But Jesus himself did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
You yourselves are my witnesses that I said, ‘I am not the Messiah, but I have been sent ahead of him.’
For the one whom God has sent speaks God's words, because God does not give the Spirit in a limited measure.
Come and see a man who told me everything I have done. Could he be the Messiah?
In these lay a large crowd of sick people, blind people, people who were lame, and people with withered limbs. They were waiting for the water to move.
Truly, truly, I tell you: the hour is coming, and is already here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who hear will live.
And he also gave him authority to carry out judgment.
Search the Scriptures, in which you think you have eternal life. They testify about me.
But I know you: you do not have the love of God in you.
Large crowds followed him because they saw the signs he was performing on the sick.
Now the Jewish Passover festival was near.
Philip said to him, “Two hundred denarii worth of bread would not be enough for them, even if each one took just a little.”
When the crowd saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they got into these boats and came to Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
They were saying, “Isn't this Jesus, Joseph's son, whose father and mother we know? How can he say, ‘I came down from heaven’?”
Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God; he has seen the Father.
Many of his disciples who heard this said, “This statement is hard. Who can listen to it?”
And we have believed and have come to know that you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
But now you are seeking to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
His neighbors and those who had previously seen him begging were saying, “Isn't this the man who used to sit and beg?”
There was again a division among the Jews because of these words.
Many people came to him and said, “John did not perform even one sign, but everything John said about this man is true.”
His disciples said to him, “Our Lord, if he is asleep, he will recover.”
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even if he dies.”
The chief priests and the Pharisees had ordered that if anyone knew where he was, they should report it to them so that they could arrest him.
The crowds said to him, “We have heard from the Law that the Messiah remains forever. How can you say that the Son of Man is to be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
So that the words of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, who said, “Lord, who has believed our message? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew that the hour had come for him to leave this world and go to his Father. He loved his own who were in this world, and he loved them to the end.
One of his disciples, the one Jesus loved, was reclining against his chest.
After the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you are doing, do quickly.”
If you knew me, you would also know my Father. From now on you know him and have seen him.
Jesus said to him, “I have been with you all this time, and you have not known me, Philip? Whoever sees me has seen the Father. How can you say, ‘Show us the Father’?”
Believe that I am in my Father and my Father is in me. Otherwise, believe at least because of the works.
If you ask me in my name, I will do it.
If anyone does not remain in me, he is thrown outside like a branch that dries up. They gather it and throw it into the fire to be burned.
I still have much to tell you, but you cannot take it in now.
In a little while you will not see me, and again in a little while you will see me, because I am going to the Father.
Now we know that you know everything and do not need anyone to question you. Because of this, we believe that you came from God.
Jesus said to them, “Believe.”
I have given them the glory you gave me, so that they may be one, just as we are one.
They answered him, “If he were not doing evil things, we would not have handed him over to you.”
Pilate said to him, “Am I a Jew? Your own people and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
The soldiers wove a crown of thorns and put it on his head, and they clothed him in purple garments.
They said, “Greetings, King of the Jews!” and struck him on his cheeks.
And he said to that disciple, “Here is your mother.” From that hour, that disciple took her into his home.
The one who saw it has testified, and his testimony is true. He knows that he has spoken the truth, so that you too may believe.
Jesus said to her, “Do not come near me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father. But go to my brothers and tell them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God.’”

When evening came on that day, the first day of the week, the doors where the disciples were staying were shut for fear of the Jews. Jesus came and stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
When morning came, Jesus stood beside the sea, but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
